text:
Championship roundup: Southampton get Larin lift as Norwich win five in a row
Southampton 2-0 Derby; Norwich 2-1 Cardiff
QPR get first away win since August at 10-man Millwall
Cyle Larin returned to action with a bang as Southampton extended their unbeaten run at home in the Championship to 18 games with a 2-0 victory over second-bottom Derby.
Larin turned in his eighth goal of the season but his first since 12 September – after a four-game drought and a hamstring problem. Divin Mubama added a second in stoppage time as Saints shrugged off worries of failing against lower-placed sides – having dropped points against Watford, Preston, Wrexham, Lincoln and Bolton already this season.
But for their four-point deduction for Spygate, the result would have taken Southampton top for at least a couple of hours. Derby would wind up bottom if Preston pulled off an unlikely win at West Ham.
Norwich came from behind to beat Cardiff 2-1 and make it five straight Championship victories – after losing their previous five. The Canaries went behind just after the break when Yousef Salech got on the end of a free-kick from deep but the visitors were quickly back on level terms as Paris Maghoma scored for the fourth game running.
Mathias Kvistgaarden then tapped home in the 68th minute after his penalty had been kept out by Nathan Trott. Ronan Kpakio had been penalised for bringing down Andre Brooks. Cardiff performed gamely all afternoon but were unable to get the equaliser their gutsy performance probably deserved.
Nicolas Madsen’s scruffy winner gave Queens Park Rangers their first away victory since August as they defeated Millwall 1-0 at the Den. The result against their London rivals ensured the Hoops will end the weekend inside the playoff places after they played the majority of the contest against 10 men following Zak Sturge’s 15th-minute red card. Sturge was shown a straight red card for tripping Paul Smyth just outside the area as the last defender.
QPR took the lead in first-half stoppage time as Lukas Jensen first saved from Ilias Chair before Madsen’s follow-up crossed the line despite Caleb Taylor’s attempted heroics. Despite a commendable defensive performance with depleted numbers, this was a third straight defeat for Millwall whose campaign continues to stutter.
Later kick-offs include Birmingham, the leaders, at Stoke, Middlesbrough in second at home to Bristol City and third-placed Wolves hosting Charlton.
